title: Oral Presentations
description: Learn to prepare and deliver effective presentations in English.
competenceGoals: express himself/herself fluently and coherently, adapted to the purpose and situation
use central patterns for pronunciation, vocabulary and sentence structure

content.content:
# Oral Presentations

Giving presentations is an important skill. Whether for school, work, or other contexts,
being able to speak clearly and confidently in English will help you succeed.

content.title: Presentation Structure
content.content:
A good presentation has three parts:

**1. Introduction** (10%)
- Greet your audience
- Introduce your topic
- Tell them what you will cover

**2. Body** (80%)
- Main points with examples
- Logical order
- Transitions between sections

**3. Conclusion** (10%)
- Summarize main points
- End memorably
- Thank the audience

content.title: Useful Phrases
content.content:
## Opening
- *"Good morning/afternoon, everyone."*
- *"Today I'm going to talk about..."*
- *"I'd like to begin by..."*

## Transitions
- *"Moving on to my next point..."*
- *"Now let's look at..."*
- *"This brings me to..."*

## Closing
- *"In conclusion..."*
- *"To sum up..."*
- *"Thank you for listening. Any questions?"*

content.title: Dealing with Nerves
content.content:
Feeling nervous is normal! Try these tips:
- **Practice** many times before the real presentation
- **Breathe** slowly and deeply before you start
- **Pause** if you need to collect your thoughts
- **Look** at friendly faces in the audience
- **Remember**: The audience wants you to succeed!

content.title: Common Mistakes
content.content:
Avoid these presentation pitfalls:
- Reading directly from your notes/screen
- Speaking too fast
- Not making eye contact
- Using too much text on slides
- Not practicing beforehand
- Going over the time limit

exercise.task: Which phrase is best for STARTING a presentation?

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.task: Choose the best opening phrase for a presentation.

exercise.solution: This phrase introduces your topic at the start.

exercise.task: Which is NOT good presentation practice?

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.solution: Reading your entire speech from notes
multipleChoiceOptions: Reading your entire speech from notes
Making eye contact with the audience

exercise.solution: Reading directly makes you seem unprepared and breaks connection with the audience.

subTasks.label: a
subTasks.task: Choose a topic you know well (hobby, favorite book/film, place you've visited).
subTasks.solution: Pick something you can speak about with enthusiasm.
multipleChoiceOptions: Pick something you can speak about with enthusiasm.
Choose a topic you know nothing about.
Pick the most boring topic possible.
Select a topic that requires no preparation.

subTasks.label: b
subTasks.task: Write an introduction with: greeting, topic, and preview of your main points.
subTasks.solution: Example: "Good morning. Today I'm going to talk about surfing. I'll cover why I started, what equipment you need, and my favorite surf spots."
multipleChoiceOptions: Example: "Good morning. Today I'm going to talk about surfing. I'll cover why I started, what equipment you need, and my favorite surf spots."

subTasks.label: c
subTasks.task: List 3 main points with one example or detail for each.
subTasks.solution: Each point should be supported by specific information.
multipleChoiceOptions: Each point should be supported by specific information.

subTasks.label: d
subTasks.task: Write a conclusion that summarizes and thanks the audience.
subTasks.solution: Briefly restate main points and end with "Thank you for listening."
multipleChoiceOptions: Briefly restate main points and end with "Thank you for listening."
Add new information in the conclusion.

hints: Keep each point simple enough to remember
